chunks: 5038 - And in the narration of Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, that ʿAlī عليه السلام said:
There is no compensation upon a fornicator, and there is no hadd punishment upon a woman who was coerced.

key_terms.زَانٍ: a fornicator; one who commits zina
key_terms.عُقْرٌ: compensation payment in this legal context
key_terms.مُسْتَكْرَهَةٍ: a woman who was coerced or compelled

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hadd punishment for a woman coerced into zina?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling in cases of zina. It states that no ʿuqr compensation is due upon the fornicator, and that a woman who was compelled is not subject to the hadd punishment, affirming the distinction between coercion and culpable action in Islamic law.
